first.rationale: Onboarding simplification directly addresses the simultaneous declines in completion and activation, with prior evidence of durable activation and adoption gains. I would verify memory_86 for downstream qualified-revenue effects and memory_73 to compare promotional pricing's acquisition lift against possible retention, account-quality, and discount-dependence risks before committing.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified precedent improved completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%, directly addressing both current declines while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Promotional pricing is rejected despite acquisition lift because its verified cohort suffered 12% lower 30-day retention and failed to survive the first renewal cycle. Uncertainty remains about effect size in the current population, so retain an experimental holdout rather than roll out broadly.
